rawModelResponse.episodeSummary: The patient, a 70-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, and heart failure, presented with generalized weakness after missing two dialysis sessions. He was found to have symptomatic bradycardia with a heart rate of 34 bpm, hypotension (MAP 59 mmHg), and ECG findings consistent with complete heart block (wide QRS, AV dissociation, peaked T waves, progressive QRS widening). Laboratory results show critical hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L), hypocalcemia (7.6 mg/dL), metabolic acidosis (pH 7.24, bicarbonate 15 mmol/L), and significantly elevated creatinine (9.8 mg/dL) and BUN (88 mg/dL), consistent with severe renal impairment. The Phase 6 analysis confirms a low heart rate (median 34.1 bpm) during the controlled event, but notes low confidence in the QRS measurement validity.
rawModelResponse.detectedEpisodeContext: Symptomatic bradycardia secondary to complete heart block in the setting of severe renal failure, electrolyte abnormalities (hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia), and metabolic acidosis, likely related to missed hemodialysis.
rawModelResponse.mostLikelyEtiology: Severe hyperkalemia secondary to end-stage renal disease and missed hemodialysis, leading to conduction system dysfunction and complete heart block.
uncertaintyAndMissingData: Phase 6 analysis has low confidence in the controlled-event heart rate measurement validity.
